evidence.publisher: Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Finance / Josef Fink
evidence.location: A review of the Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift (2021), §1.2 and Observation 2, paragraphs on SUE and zero-investment quantile portfolios
evidence.trade_description: Review describes highest-vs-lowest standardized unexpected earnings decile portfolios with long positive and short negative earnings surprises. 60-trading-day and published excess-return claims are historical literature, not system results.
evidence.limitations: Review is not a brokerage execution manual; real earnings surprise timestamp, survivorship-free universe and borrow availability are required.

source_confirmed_rules.rule: High standardized earnings surprise stocks are the long portfolio; low surprise stocks are the short portfolio as a research design.
source_confirmed_rules.source_location: Fink review §1.2, Observation 2: highest and lowest earnings surprise decile; historical literature not algorithm parameters.

research_assumptions.basis: Fixture execution duration only; not the paper's optimal holding period.
Equal gross-notional test sizing chosen by developer.
Use decile ranking as review's literature convention; exact data construction and edge conditions assumed.
No look-ahead illustrative execution rule, not a quoted research fill assumption.
Not provided or verified; net profitability deliberately unknown.

legs.definition: select highest observed pre-trade SUE among real eligible universe
select lowest observed pre-trade SUE with verified borrow
